_about: The effects the original's script ADDS - entities spawned by name with AddEntity - as each call
adds its one: which .ent, where from the point the call is given, at what depth, turned how and
at what scale. The call site's facts only: what the entity itself is (its sprite, its particle
systems, its light, its own <Scale>) is read from the original's .ent at run time by
Art::LoadEnt and never copied here, since hand copies of the fifty-odd files would drift.
Decoded from android_game.bin through the remake's asbc listing (out/parity/asbc/
all_functions.txt, md5 48fe65ce8baea16b94ed84d8d7be84b0). Step 91 of
docs/planning/2026-09-11-magic-portals-remaster.md (the visuals plan's 6.2, system_7 7a-1).
WHAT IS HERE. The rows of vanishEffect and appearEffect (Portal.angelscript), whose
arithmetic test_mp_effects pins: the teleport's three effects, drawn by the visuals plan's
step 7.3. The fireball and its two explosions (7.2). The two entities PortalManager::
insertPortal adds for every portal a shot opens, the burst ETHCallback_portal leaves where
one dies, and that callback's own colours and clocks in placed_portal (7.4). And red_eyes,
MainCharacter's own, drawn by step 7.1 - added once at a level's
start rather than at a call site, so it has a shape and a reader of its own. Every other
effect the script adds gets its row with the step that draws it, so a
missing row is an effect not yet drawn, not one the script lacks. What reads a row is
sim/Effects, strictly: every field below is required.
UNITS. AddEntity(file, vector3(xy, z), angle, @out, altName, scale), its arguments pushed
last-first (00_order 8.0 rule 3; ETHScriptWrapper.Scene.cpp:131-158). The script's
g_scale.scale(n) is n x screenHeight / 256 (00_order 8.12a), which is n of the port's units,
so offset_units and a z whose `scaled` is true are those n. A z the call writes as a bare
literal is in the engine's own units and does not grow with the screen (00_order 8.12b):
`scaled` false says so; the port, whose unit is one level unit, reads the number as it is.
`scale` is a multiple of g_scale.getScale(), the script's scale for anything it adds at its
own size, which is 1 in the port's units; the entity is drawn at that times its .ent's
<Scale> (Art::Entity::ScaleAt). `angle` is Ethanon's, in degrees, counter-clockwise on the
screen: a number, or the named rule toward_traveller_minus_90, radianToDegree(getAngle(d)) -
90 with d = normalize(traveller - portal) and getAngle(v) = atan2f(v.x, v.y) wrapped into
[0, 2 pi) (GameMath.h:711-715), computed in floats as the script computes it.

_source: explosion.ent is an .ent of the original's that nothing adds: the listing holds no string
'explosion.ent' (its explosion names are 'explosion_large.ent', 'small_explosion.ent',
'small_explosion_no_light.ent' and 'antiportal_explosion.ent'), and no level places it -
no <EntityName> or custom-data value of any of the 133 .esc files names it. A barrel's
blast is explode()'s explosion_large.ent (MiscCallbacks, bytes 342023..342895, #23;
ETHCallback_barrel_bomb #56-60), which is what the plan's 7e row 'explosion.ent /
explosion_large.ent on barrel detonations' should read (system_7 S10).
vanishEffect (Portal.angelscript, bytes 356384..356958), called with the traveller's
position before it moves and the entry portal's: #2-13 direction = normalize(objectPos -
portalPos) (normalize of a zero vector is zero, GameMath.h:755-761); #14-26 offset =
direction x g_scale.scale(32); #28-34 angle = radianToDegree(getAngle(direction)) - 90;
#36-69 AddEntity('suck_effect.ent', vector3(portalPos + offset, g_scale.scale(32)),
angle, @effect, '', g_scale.getScale()). Its callers: PortalManager::teleportToOther
(bytes 144944..145873) #61, before #69 moves the traveller;
PortalManager::teleportToFirstStaticPortal (145999..146550) #44;
ETHCallback_portal_static (360571..361404) #144; and LoadingScreen::loop
(178170..179373) #241 - the loading screen, which ui.json's loading.vanish reads with
the same 32 and -90 (test_mp_effects pins that the two agree).
vanishEffect #83-112: AddEntity('sparkles.ent', vector3(objectPos, g_scale.scale(32)),
angle, @effect, '', g_scale.getScale()) - at the traveller where it stood, turned as the
suck effect is (#93 pushes the same local). #100-101: VAR objectPos then GETOBJREF 0,
which names the stack slot VAR just filled, not the portal (00_order 8.0 rule 1).
appearEffect (Portal.angelscript, bytes 357060..357278), called with the exit portal's
position once the traveller stands there (teleportToOther #71-75, after #69):
AddEntity('appear_effect.ent', vector3(pos, 2), 0, @effect, '', g_scale.getScale()) -
#12 the angle 0, #13 the z 2, a bare literal (PshC4 2f, not through g_scale.scale). The
same pair of calls ends teleportToFirstStaticPortal (#44, #58) and ETHCallback_portal_static
Beholder's spawnStone (bytes 373491..373647) adds the same .ent at a rock another way,
AddScaledEntity('appear_effect.ent', vector3(pos, 0), g_scale.scale(1.5)) (#5-22): z 0
and scale 1.5, a row of its own for the step that draws the rocks' effect.
addFireball (ETHCallback_carranca.angelscript, bytes 417483..417923), the one function
that makes a fireball, whoever asks for it: #12-17 vector3(pos, 0f) - two bare literals,
the angle and the z, neither through g_scale.scale - and #19-26 AddEntity('fireball.ent',
that, 0, @entity, '', g_scale.getScale()), so the entity is added at its own size and the
1.2 it is drawn at is its .ent's own <Scale>. It then writes killMainCharacter (#40-53)
and dir (#57-65) on the entity, clears its gravity (#69-74) and plays the spit sound.
ITS FOUR CALLERS: carrancaCallback #108, at the gargoyle's GetPositionXY along its own
(dirX, dirY); burnProjectile #54, where a fire diamond turns a portal shot into one;
ETHCallback_dragon #754 (2-32); and ETHCallback_dark_dragon #978 and #1720 (4-32). The
first three pass fireballScale 1 and the dark dragon 2 (PshC4 2f at #972 and #1714),
which is the one argument that is not the same for all of them: #77-83 calls
ScaleParticleSystem(0, fireballScale) when it is not 1, so it scales system 0 ALONE and
on top of the entity's own <Scale>. The port carries it per fireball
(Turrets::Fireball::particle_scale) and darkdragon.json's fight.fireball_particle_scale
holds the 2.
IT IS NOT TEMPORARY. fireball.ent's one system repeats 0 - forever - so
ETHEntity::IsTemporary is false and the engine never deletes it: it goes when its script
deletes it (ETHCallback_fireball below), which the port models as the effect going when
the fireball it follows goes.
ETHCallback_fireball (ETHCallback_carranca.angelscript, bytes 418524..418930), the
fireball's own per-frame callback: #44-56 it reads its `destroy` flag, and when it is set
#57-65 DeleteEntity(thisEntity) and #66-83 AddScaledEntity('small_explosion.ent',
thisEntity.GetPosition(), g_scale.getScale()) - the fireball's own vector3, whose z is
the 0 addFireball gave it, at the script's own size. AddScaledEntity is AddEntity(file,
pos, 0f, 0, '', scale) (ETHScriptWrapper.Scene.cpp:176-178), so the angle is 0 and the
0.8 it is drawn at is the .ent's <Scale>. #84-87 also startEarthquake(5, 0), which the
port has no earthquake for.
WHAT SETS `destroy`: ETHBeginContactCallback_fireball (418930..419710) alone. A character
the fireball cannot kill returns at #10-31; a carranca or a sensor that is not a
shock_agent returns at #98-121; everything else reaches #146-152 destroy(thisEntity) -
so a shock agent, a burnable, a bomb, the player it kills, AND ANY SOLID IT TOUCHES.
The port's fireball is a bare point with no body, so it records the first four
(Turrets::State::spent_px) and flies through walls; Turrets.hpp says why a body is its
own step. Neither of the port's other two removals adds one: the cull at the level's edge
is the port's own, and a torch's switch goes through killProjectile (MiscCallbacks,
351788..351878), a bare DeleteEntity that sets no flag.
explode (MiscCallbacks.angelscript, bytes 342023..342895) #1-23:
AddScaledEntity('explosion_large.ent', vector3(pos, g_scale.scale(32)),
g_scale.scale(superScale)) - the z through g_scale.scale, so 32 level units, and the
scale g_scale.scale of the caller's superScale, which is 1 of the port's units per
superScale of 1. Then #27-31 playExplosionSound and #33-47 an EntityGrabber of
g_scale.scale(80) over the real colliders, which Fire::Blast already models.
A BARREL passes superScale 1 (ETHCallback_barrel_bomb #56-60), which is every blast the
port makes: Fire::State::blasts_px is where they went off. Its other callers -
fire_agent #191, beholder #1274, dark_dragon #1931, the fireball's contact #188, ghost
#1352 and explode itself #137 for a chain - are not built as blasts here, and each
brings its own scale with the step that builds it.
explosion.ent is NEVER spawned (see _never_spawned above): the plan's 'explosion.ent /
explosion_large.ent' is one entity, this one.
PortalManager::insertPortal (PortalManager.angelscript, bytes 142281..142841) #4-33, the first of
the two entities a placed portal is made of: #14-19 vector3(pos, g_scale.scale(32)) and #26-33
AddEntity('portal_summon_effect.ent', that, 0, @out, '', g_scale.getScale()). The bubble that
announces a new portal, added BEFORE portal.ent (#71), which is the order the two draw their
random in.
ITS .ent: no <Sprite>, one system of 1 onda.png, a1 rep1, life 500, size 33, growth +6.4, minSize
16, colour (0.9, 0.7, 1) to black - a ring that GROWS where the teleport's appear_effect shrinks.
The footage measures it at 382 u/s on the clearer of its two rings against the .ent's 384
(out/parity/footage/F2.md section 4.3). Temporary, so the engine frees it once its pool is over.
insertPortal #47-71: AddEntity('portal.ent', vector3(pos, 0f), 0f, @portal, 'portal.ent',
g_scale.getScale()) - the PORTAL ITSELF, an entity like any other the script adds, with the
alternative name that makes SeekEntity find it. Both the angle and the z are bare literals
(PshC4 0f at #57 and #58), and 0 is 0 on either reading.
ITS .ent: <Sprite>portal_halo.png</Sprite> at blendMode 1 (added), applyLight 0, emissive
(1, 1, 1); sys0 4 x portal_spiral.png, a1 rep0, life 900 +- 450, size 70, growth -0.8, angleDir
1.3, <StartPoint> z 10; sys1 1 x portal.png, a0 rep0, life 100, size 64, <StartPoint> z 10; and
<CustomData> speed 1, stride 2, which are linearMotion's (placement.json portal.bob).
IT IS NOT TEMPORARY - both systems repeat 0 - so nothing but ETHCallback_portal deletes it,
which is what placed_portal below writes down.
ETHCallback_portal (Portal.angelscript, bytes 359141..359885) #159-176:
AddScaledEntity('portal_death.ent', thisEntity.GetPosition(), g_scale.getScale()), at the portal's
own vector3 - whose z is the 0 insertPortal gave it - on the frame its kill clock passes 400 ms,
immediately before #177-185 DeleteEntity(thisEntity). AddScaledEntity is AddEntity(file, pos, 0f,
0, '', scale), so the angle is 0.
ITS .ent: no <Sprite>, 4 x explosion.png cut 4 x 3, a1 rep1, all at once, life 300 +- 300, size
48, growth +0.6, maxSize 92, <StartPoint> z 4. Temporary.
ETHCallback_light_off #139 and ETHCallback_fire_signal #242 add the same .ent at a projectile;
those are the torch's steps, not this one.
WHAT ETHEntity::SetColor DOES TO A PLACED PORTAL, and what the kill fade then multiplies.
PortalManager::update (bytes 138545..139692) recolours its array every frame, AFTER popping any
portal whose systems have been killed (#165-180, #230-246):
#185-188 size > 1: #192-207 portals[0] = PORTAL_RED, #212-227 portals[1] = PORTAL_BLUE.
#248-259 size == 1 and maxPortals == 1: #264-279 portals[0] = PORTAL_RED.
#282-300 size == 1 otherwise: portals[0] = V3_ZERO.
Nothing colours index 2 or beyond, and nothing recolours a portal once it has been popped.
PORTAL_RED (1, 0.3, 0.4) and PORTAL_BLUE (0.3, 0.4, 1) are global initialisers (listing lines
60476 and 60485); V3_ZERO is (0, 0, 0). 00_order section 8.2 (decode D1) cites the same four
call sites while ruling the STATIC portal's own tint out of them.
BLACK IS NOT A BUG. portal.ent's sprite is additive, so colour (0, 0, 0) adds nothing and the
halo simply does not draw: a lone portal on a level that grants two is its spiral and its iris
and nothing else, which is what the original's still shows (out/parity/smoke/nav/01, 1-3) and
what F2 measures as 'no halo tint' until the second portal opens (section 4.4).
ONLY THE SPRITE TAKES IT. SetColor writes m_v4Color (ETHEntity.cpp:493-498), the sprite draws
min(1, ambient + emissive) x m_v4Color (ETHRenderEntity.cpp:112-117), and the particle pass
draws particle.color x ambient alone (ETHParticleManager.cpp:381-389). So the spiral and the
iris are never tinted and never fade with the halo.
THE KILL FADE. ETHCallback_portal #127-142: once its killTime is set, SetColor(GetColor() x 0.9)
EVERY FRAME; #144-158, once GetTime() - killTime passes 400 ms, portal_death and DeleteEntity.
The 0.9 is per rendered frame of a game that ran at the device's rate, so the port applies it
per 1/60 s of frame time (kill_fade_frame_ms): an INFERRED reading that makes a 120 Hz run match
a 60 Hz one, and the only one of these six numbers that is not read straight off an instruction.
killTime is READ BEFORE IT IS WRITTEN (#99-101 against #113-123), so the frame that sets it
neither fades nor counts; both start on the frame after.
MainCharacter's own effect, and the one effect every level shows. It is NOT a call site
of the shape above: AddScaledEntity takes no angle and no direction, and the entity is
added once and then moved every frame, so its row is read by its own reader.
MainCharacter::MainCharacter (bytes 126650..127790) #85-101 AddScaledEntity('red_eyes.ent',
entity.GetPosition(), g_scale.getScale()) and #105-119 SeekEntity('red_eyes.ent') into the
redEyes handle: at the level's start, on every level, at the character's own point and its
own depth. AddScaledEntity is AddEntity(file, pos, 0f, 0, '', scale) (Ethanon
ETHScriptWrapper.Scene.cpp:176-178), so the angle is 0.
MainCharacter::updateEyes (bytes 134329..134672), run first thing every frame by
MainCharacter::update #4, before its own pause test: #6 if the character is NOT hidden,
#15-22 eyeX = GetFrame() > 7 ? 7f : -7f; #24-31 eyeY = noGravity ? -15.65f : -14.25f;
#33-64 redEyes.SetPosition(entity.GetPosition() + g_scale.scale(vector3(eyeX, eyeY, 1f)));
#66-72 otherwise redEyes.Hide(true) (SetV1's second operand is an 8-bit immediate, so
#67 is the literal 1). GetFrame is the cell in dark_mage.ent's 4 x 4 sheet, and rows 2
and 3 - frames 8-15, walking right and pushing right - are the ones above 7 (art.json
rows_by_direction).
UNITS. The vector3 overload of g_scale.scale (bytes 5975..6072) is vector3::opMul_r of
the scale factor, which multiplies all three components, so 7, -14.25, -15.65 and the z 1
are all in level units. The z is added to the CHARACTER's depth (art.json character.z over
the level's scale factor), not to the level's zero.
THE ENTITY ITSELF is red_eyes.ent, read at run time by Art::LoadEnt: no <Sprite>, one
<ParticleSystem> of 12 hard_halo.png at alphaMode 1, repeat 0, life 120 +- 100 ms, size 4
growing -0.03, colour (1, 0.1, 0.1) to black, <StartPoint> z 2. Repeat 0 makes it NOT
temporary (Art::Entity::Temporary), so the engine never deletes it and it lives as long as
the character does.
HIDE_WITH_PLAYER IS A RECORDED FACT AND NOT A KNOB. It has exactly one legal value: Effects::LoadRules
refuses a row that says false, because the port's player owner both moves the eyes and hides them, and a
row that said otherwise would need an owner of its own. The field writes down #66-72 redEyes.Hide(true)
beside the arithmetic it belongs to; it is not a number a designer retunes.
